floors.content: If a railway track is not a true line, what is it? In math, it is called a line segment. A segment just has a hard start and a hard stop. Because it has two ends, you can easily measure it with a ruler. Almost everything we see, draw, or build in the physical world is a line segment.

Then there is a ray. A ray has a starting point, but no ending point. It just keeps going in one direction. Think of turning on a strong flashlight in the dark. The beam starts right there at the bulb, but the light just shoots outward. It has a beginning, but it does not stop.

Finally, if you take away that starting point too, you are back to a true line. The whole difference between the three concepts just comes down to counting the ends. A segment has two ends. A ray has one end. A true line has zero ends. That is really all there is to it.
